newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HORNETS STING HOME-HAPPY HAWKS IN ATLANTA.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HORNETS STING HOME-HAPPY HAWKS IN ATLANTA.

text.p: Tony Smith's layup with 15 seconds left, off a beautiful pass through the key by Tony Delk, lifted the Charlotte Hornets to their fourth straight victory, 93-92 over the Atlanta Hawks on Saturday.
Smith, who had just four points, cut under the hoop and Delk found him with a bullet pass from the top of the three-point arc for the winning basket.
"I just had a man wide open, it was the right thing to do at that moment," Delk said of the game-winning pass. "I was a little surprised, it happened so fast."
Anthony Mason led the Hornets with 25 points and 12 rebounds.
Christian Laettner had 24 points and 16 rebounds for the Hawks, who lost for just the second time in their last 24 home games.

"I think we did a good job fighting back the whole game," Laettner said. "We were down by 16 points and showed a lot of heart by hanging in there and actually taking the lead. But after you come back from a deficit like that you don't want to let it slip away."
"Our guys are so determined not to lose, sometimes their will to win is remarkable," Hornets coach Dave Cowens said.
The Hornets (34-21) moved within two games of the third place Hawks (35-18) in the Central Division.
In Chicago, Michael Jordan scored 34 points and keyed a pair of third-quarter runs as the Chicago Bulls routed the Golden State Warriors 120-87 for their sixth straight win.

Scottie Pippen had 22 points and Toni Kukoc added 15 points and 10 rebounds for the Bulls, who have won 14 of their last 15 games. Dennis Rodman grabbed 12 rebounds for the NBA champion Bulls (48-6), who are a league-best 25-1 at home.
Joe Smith scored 19 points and Latrell Sprewell added 18 for Golden State, who have not beaten Chicago since November 1991.
In Dallas, Doug Christie scored 22 points and Walt Williams added seven of his 14 in a key fourth-quarter run as the Toronto Raptors claimed their first-ever win in Dallas, 99-92 over the Mavericks.
Damon Stoudamire added 15 points and nine assists for the Raptors, who won for just the second time in eight games. The Raptors made 12 of 18 field goals in the fourth quarter.

Recently acquired guard Sasha Danilovic scored 20 points for Dallas. He left after suffering an apparent ankle injury in the final minute. Michael Finley also had 20 points and Shawn Bradley added 19 and 11 rebounds for the new-look Mavs, who dropped to 1-3 since their nine-player deal with the Nets.

In Philadelphia, Derrick Coleman scored 13 of his 28 points in the first quarter and grabbed 15 rebounds as the Philadelphia 76ers posted their second straight win, 97-80 over the Portland Trail Blazers.
Jerry Stackhouse added 21 points and Allen Iverson 18 for Philadelphia, which recorded consecutive wins for just the second time since November 30.

Kenny Anderson scored 20 points and Clifford Robinson added 16 for Portland, losers of seven of their last eight road games. Rasheed Wallace was held to 10 points for the Trail Blazers, who never led.
